note: Teaching text, clarifying questions, inferred constraints and own examples. Inferred, not official. Examples are small generated inputs with outputs from the independent references in oracles.py.

clarifyingQuestions: Must the match in y be contiguous?
What is returned when nothing matches?
Can either string be empty?
hints: Fix where the substring of y ends; then it only grows to the left.
dp[i][j]: the longest substring of y ending at position j that is a subsequence of x[:i].
If x[i-1] = y[j-1], extend dp[i-1][j-1] by one; otherwise skip x[i-1] and keep dp[i-1][j].
invariants: dp[i][j] <= min(i, j)
dp[i][j] is non-decreasing in i
chooseWhen: One side must stay contiguous and the other may skip characters
tradeoffs: The quadratic table is simple but needs a rolling row to keep memory at O(|y|)
hack2hire:6a0237332608e589a944a2be.variantLabel: Inferred: subsequence of x matched against a substring of y

clarifyingQuestions: What happens to a query whose point is occupied, or whose two neighbours are both occupied?
Is an answer reported after a skipped query?
Can positions be negative?
hints: A new house touches at most the run ending just left of it or the run starting just right of it; the build rule forbids touching both, so runs never merge.
Store run lengths at both endpoints of every run; interior points never need updating.
The longest run never shrinks, so keep a running maximum.
invariants: for every maximal run [l, r], length[l] = length[r] = r - l + 1
the answer sequence is non-decreasing
chooseWhen: Points are sparse or unbounded, so an array indexed by position is impractical
tradeoffs: Union-find also works but needs path compression; endpoint lengths are O(1) per insertion without it
hack2hire:69a351986e73e4abccc9bf81.variantLabel: Inferred: running longest run with a skipped-query rule

clarifyingQuestions: Is case significant?
What is returned for the empty string?
hints: A bad triple ends at index i when s[i] = s[i-1] = s[i-2].
No valid window may contain both i - 2 and i, so the next window starts at i - 1.
Track the start and update the best length at every index.
invariants: the window [start, i] never contains three equal consecutive characters
chooseWhen: The forbidden pattern is local (a fixed-length run)
tradeoffs: A run-length view also works but needs more bookkeeping
hack2hire:6854ca09c201117d348a25d5.variantLabel: Inferred: longest window without a triple

clarifyingQuestions: Are all elements positive?
What if no element fits?
hints: With positive elements, shrinking the window always lowers the sum.
For each right end, the best left end is the smallest one whose window sum is at most k.
That left end only moves right, so a two-pointer window is linear.
invariants: window sum <= k after shrinking
left <= right + 1
tradeoffs: Fails for negative elements, where prefix sums plus a monotonic structure are needed
hack2hire:6a974f580ca9cc4e1c789f3b.variantLabel: Inferred: longest window with bounded sum

clarifyingQuestions: Do letters absent from s count?
Is a letter in only one case valid?
hints: Only the last lowercase and first uppercase occurrence of each letter matter.
A letter qualifies when it has no lowercase, no uppercase, or last lowercase < first uppercase.
Record both positions in one pass and count at the end.
invariants: lastLower[c] and firstUpper[c] describe the scanned prefix
chooseWhen: Order constraints between two classes of occurrences
tradeoffs: Pairwise comparison is simpler but quadratic
hack2hire:67fbdd34216af53465a721a5.variantLabel: Inferred: count letters with lowercase strictly before uppercase

constraints: timestamps are digit strings with non-decreasing values
clarifyingQuestions: What is the output format?
What happens when a sell exceeds the holding?
Is cash allowed to go negative?
hints: Keep cash as an integer and holdings in a hash map.
Clamp a sell to the shares held and drop symbols that reach zero.
Sort the symbols only once, when building the output.
invariants: cash = 1000 - total spent + total received
every stored holding is positive
chooseWhen: Replaying a ledger with keyed balances
tradeoffs: A sorted map would keep order continuously but costs log time per trade
hack2hire:67d266555e44a1b0c201ee79.variantLabel: Inferred level 1: replay trades into a portfolio

constraints: timestamps are digit strings with non-decreasing values
clarifyingQuestions: Which price does a margin sale use?
How are ties between equal prices broken?
What if selling everything does not cover the deficit?
hints: Margin selling never changes prices, so the chosen symbol stays best until it is exhausted or cash is covered.
Selling one share at a time from one symbol equals selling ceil(deficit / price) shares at once.
Use a heap keyed by (-latest price, symbol) and skip stale entries.
invariants: heap entries whose price or holding no longer match are ignored
after a margin call, cash >= 0 or no shares are held
chooseWhen: Repeated greedy picks of a maximum under updates
tradeoffs: A full rescan per margin sale is simpler but quadratic

constraints: timestamps are digit strings with non-decreasing values
clarifyingQuestions: Which symbols are options, and on which stock?
May collateral be sold during a margin call?
Does selling an option free stock shares immediately?
hints: A stock is sellable only above its option count; an option is always sellable.
If the best sellable symbol is an option whose stock has a higher (or equal) price, every option sale unlocks one stock share that is then sold next.
Sell options alone until both counts are equal, then alternate option and stock; compute how many of each in closed form.
invariants: options sold during a margin call never leave a stock below zero sellable shares
the chosen best symbol stays best until exhausted, covered, or (for an option) its stock unlocks
tradeoffs: Share-by-share simulation is obviously right but costs O(shares) per call
hack2hire:67d2675c5e44a1b0c201ee7b.variantLabel: Inferred level 3: margin calls with option collateral

clarifyingQuestions: Are repeated values counted once?
What is the frame of a 2 x 2 square?
Can values be negative?
hints: Only the border cells of each square matter; inner cells are ignored.
Each frame has 4k - 4 cells for k >= 2 and one cell for k = 1.
Walk the border directly instead of filtering the whole square.
invariants: each frame visit adds each border cell exactly once to the set
tradeoffs: Distinctness prevents sliding-window sums; recomputing each frame is simplest at these bounds
hack2hire:6a1c7cfc8b879849ebc0f85d.variantLabel: Inferred: best frame by sum of distinct border values

clarifyingQuestions: Do tasks that touch at an endpoint overlap?
Can a task have zero length?
hints: Finishing early leaves the most room for later tasks.
Sort by end time.
Take a task whenever it starts no earlier than the end of the last taken task.
invariants: the taken tasks are pairwise non-overlapping
lastEnd is the smallest possible end of any optimal prefix
chooseWhen: Maximising a count of compatible intervals
tradeoffs: Sorting costs O(n log n); weighted versions need DP instead
hack2hire:6827f7c3f13ac663af91d7a5.variantLabel: Inferred: interval scheduling by earliest end

clarifyingQuestions: How much does one upgrade raise the value?
Can upgrades be partial?
Must the whole budget be spent?
hints: Feasibility is monotone: if a floor is affordable, every lower floor is too.
Lifting every asset to floor T costs the sum of (T - values[i]) * costs[i] over assets below T.
Binary search T; stop summing as soon as the cost exceeds the budget.
invariants: lo is always affordable, hi + 1 never is
chooseWhen: Maximising a minimum under a monotone budget
tradeoffs: The early exit keeps sums small (exact in JavaScript) but makes the check data-dependent
hack2hire:69e933bdfbaf3da641828694.variantLabel: Inferred: binary search on the achievable floor

clarifyingQuestions: Must a and b be distinct?
How large can the range be?
hints: The range can be huge, so enumerate bits rather than numbers.
Choose the bits of a and b from the top, tracking whether each is still tight against lo and hi, whether the XOR is still tight against k, and whether a < b is decided.
A higher XOR bit beats all lower bits, so try XOR bit 1 first and memoise feasibility per state.
invariants: a state is feasible iff some completion satisfies every bound
chooseWhen: Bounded pair problems over huge integer ranges
tradeoffs: Exhaustive search is simple but only works for tiny ranges
hack2hire:6a725ef948af2ae18e995ee1.variantLabel: Inferred: digit DP over bit tightness flags

clarifyingQuestions: What exactly is combined, and what is the diversity limit?
Can health be zero or negative?
Is k the number of distinct series?
hints: With positive health, taking every server of a chosen series never hurts.
So the task reduces to picking at most k series with the largest totals.
Keep a size-k min-heap of series totals.
invariants: the heap holds the k largest totals seen so far
tradeoffs: Sorting all totals is simpler; the heap saves memory when k is small
hack2hire:676efc4fb2c9d428b406a287.variantLabel: Inferred: top-k series by total health

clarifyingQuestions: What is the score of a split?
Must both parts be non-empty?
hints: The distinct count of a prefix only grows as the prefix grows.
Precompute distinct counts for every suffix from the right.
Combine prefix count at i with suffix count at i + 1.
invariants: prefix[i] counts distinct values in arr[0..i]
chooseWhen: Two-sided aggregate over every split point
tradeoffs: Two passes and an O(n) array
hack2hire:6a724c9748af2ae18e995e5e.variantLabel: Inferred: maximise left plus right distinct counts

clarifyingQuestions: Is the answer the total profit or the chosen task list?
Does a deadline of 0 allow any task?
Are names unique?
hints: Only how many tasks finish by each deadline matters, not which second each runs.
Process tasks by increasing deadline, tentatively taking each one.
When more tasks are taken than the current deadline allows, drop the least profitable (min-heap).
invariants: the heap is always a schedulable set of maximum profit among the processed tasks
tradeoffs: Non-unit durations make this NP-hard; the heap only works for unit times
hack2hire:68c2e2221f64f4312b0a3df8.variantLabel: Inferred: unit-time job sequencing with deadlines

constraints: times are unsorted and may repeat
clarifyingQuestions: How is efficiency defined?
Can the window be empty or of zero length?
Do equal arrival times count separately?
hints: An optimal window starts and ends on arrival times.
Group equal times and sort them.
Like Kadane: extending the best window ending at the previous time costs the gap; restart when that is worse than starting fresh.
invariants: best[j] is the best efficiency of a window ending exactly at the j-th distinct time
tradeoffs: Sorting dominates; the DP itself is linear
hack2hire:6a8664a4701a76fc6843b36e.variantLabel: Inferred: tests executed minus active duration

clarifyingQuestions: How is the expression evaluated?
Is a single digit valid?
What if there is no digit?
hints: Since + and - are applied left to right, the value is the previous value plus or minus the last digit.
For both operators the best predecessor value is the maximum one.
Keep best[digit cell]; an operator cell stores the maximum best of its up/left digit neighbours.
invariants: best[i][j] is the maximum value of a valid expression ending at digit cell (i, j)
tradeoffs: If multiplication were allowed, both minimum and maximum would be needed

clarifyingQuestions: Can boards overlap?
Is L at least 1 even if all holes coincide?
hints: After sorting, one board covers a prefix and the other the remaining suffix.
For a split after index i, L must reach max(a[i] - a[0], a[n-1] - a[i+1]).
Take the minimum over splits, and at least 1 because L is positive.
invariants: a prefix/suffix split exists in some optimal cover
chooseWhen: Covering points with a fixed number of equal intervals
tradeoffs: Binary search on L also works; the direct split formula avoids it
hack2hire:67d33f6a488516fd8ad5a064.variantLabel: Inferred: two equal boards over sorted holes
